mechanism_narrative: Increasing GDP indicates strong economic activity, which should positively impact S&P 500 returns as corporate earnings are likely to improve.
failure_condition: If GDPC1 growth is positive but S&P 500 returns are negative over the 20-day horizon in more than 40% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in unemployment rate indicates labor market weakness, which could negatively affect consumer spending and thus S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: If UNRATE rises above 4% but S&P 500 returns are positive in more than 50% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: High federal funds rate coupled with low unemployment suggests tight monetary policy, which can negatively impact equity valuations.
failure_condition: If FEDFUNDS is high and UNRATE is low but S&P 500 returns are positive in more than 60% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: Increasing housing starts during an economic expansion indicate strong demand, which should positively impact S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: If HOUST increases during expansion but S&P 500 returns are negative in more than 30% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: Rising consumer price inflation may lead to tighter monetary policy, negatively impacting S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: If CPIAUCSL increases but S&P 500 returns are positive in more than 50% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production suggests supply chain issues, which could negatively impact S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: If INDPRO is below 100 but S&P 500 returns are positive in more than 40% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: Employment growth without corresponding retail sales growth indicates potential consumer weakness, negatively impacting S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: If PAYEMS increases but RSAFS does not and S&P 500 returns are positive in more than 50% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: High federal funds rate during a monetary tightening cycle may lead to decreased corporate investments and negative S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: If FEDFUNDS is above 2% during tightening but S&P 500 returns are positive in more than 40% of cases.
